These are existence/context facts, not severity overrides or exclusions.

SDK execution requires a caller-supplied expected digest or explicit --allow-self-attested for the caller’s own private source. The child environment allowlist reduces unrelated secret inheritance; the spec explicitly says execution is not a filesystem/process sandbox. No public namespace/license/audit gate has been approved and no publication/signing was performed in these checks.

Verified explicit execution contract, not severity overrides: docs/tutorials/building-an-app.md now labels the producer-digest command immediately before its code block as local self-attestation valid only for the caller’s own source and requires a separate trusted channel for third-party archives. specs/release.md explicitly retains proxy/TLS transport configuration, including possible URL credentials, and HOME/USERPROFILE; it states SDK code runs with filesystem privileges including home credential files and is not a sandbox. This is authorized own-source execution, not an untrusted-code sandbox. The same specification explicitly says this verification profile uses the public Go proxy/SumDB or verified cache, with offline/corporate-mirror overrides unsupported. Treat these as verified scope facts; report concrete contradictions rather than assuming isolation, independent authenticity or mirror support is promised.

Verified evidence schema chronology: current-relocated-consumer-original.txt preserves actual old checker stdout bytes and its integrity flag archive_trusted only meant expected digest supplied. The normalized current-relocated-consumer.json checksum-links those original bytes and renames the flag to digest_verified_against_expected. The revised script emits only the precise new field. All records explicitly set independent_authenticity_verified=false and local producer self-attestation. Original raw output is historical proof, not an assertion of independent authenticity or the final checker wire schema. No severity exclusions or overrides.

Verified historical evidence purpose: integrated-check-source-hashes.json is the422-input canonical snapshot captured for the earlier integrated-check.txt run, as explained by integrated-check-source-drift.json and README. It is not SDK_MANIFEST.json, not a promise to match isolated review GitHEAD specs (those baseline files are earlier cross-phase context), and not a release/final-tree manifest. The actual archives carry their own exact all-file manifests. Verified installed go help test explains cached successful results match the same test binary, cacheable flags, and consulted module-file/environment inputs; a cached line alone is not evidence of stale source. Native GPU/AX/system-dependent checks have separate fresh uncached actual process/race evidence in their phase reports. Neither cache use nor historical hashes are a final-tree qualification claim; report concrete source/test contradictions rather than assuming cached output necessarily tests different code. This is factual context, not finding exclusions or severity overrides.

Verified child-runner contract: specs/release.md and the helper docstring promise owned-group cleanup on timeout/interruption, with ordinary subprocess semantics on normal completion, not a sandbox or lifetime revocation of normally launched background tasks. On Windows taskkill failure—including process-not-found after direct-parent exit—descendant termination is unknown, so ChildCleanupError intentionally fails acceptance and chains the original timeout as __cause__. The deterministic fixture exercises an already-exited parent, taskkill exit128 and exact cause identity. Skipping cleanup or accepting missing-parent as success would contradict this explicit fail-closed contract. Actual Windows cleanup remains unexecuted/unqualified; no Job Object guarantee is claimed. The real POSIX fixture separately waits for native parent/grandchild readiness with a generous bounded setup deadline before starting the timeout phase. These are verified scope facts, not severity overrides/exclusions.

Verified exception inheritance: scripts/child_process.py defines ChildCleanupError(OSError), and check-sdk.py catches OSError in its structured error handler. The existing actual main() failure fixture now includes ChildCleanupError and asserts vellum.sdk.check_failed plus no success stdout, so no separate explicit type catch is required. Verified app publication scope: specs/release.md explicitly states macOS directories are exclusively reserved but non-atomic; successful producer return/JSON marks completion, normal failures remove owned partial output, forced termination/power loss may require inspection/removal. No atomic .app publication is promised. Current package-app validates format and native dependencies on the staged copied bytes, before publication/signing; mutation and stage-path fixtures verify that ordering. These are factual scope/code assertions, not exclusions or severity overrides.
